L7@P0: Abstract. The pop-stack operator of a finite lattice L is the map that sends each x in L to
L8@P0: the meet of x with the set of elements covered by x. Using tools from representation
L9@P0: theory, we provide simple Coxeter-theoretic and lattice-theoretic descriptions of the
L10@P0: image of the pop-stack operator of a Cambrian lattice of a finite irreducible Coxeter
L11@P0: group. When specialized to a bipartite Cambrian lattice of type A, this result settles a
L12@P0: conjecture of Choi and Sun. We also settle a related enumerative conjecture of Defant
L13@P0: and Williams. When L is an arbitrary lattice quotient of the weak order on W, we
L14@P0: prove that the maximum size of a forward orbit under the pop-stack operator of L is
L15@P0: at most the Coxeter number of W; when L is a Cambrian lattice, we provide an explicit
L16@P0: construction to show that this maximum forward orbit size is actually equal to the
L17@P0: Coxeter number.
L18@P0: Keywords: torsion classes, Cambrian lattice, weak order, pop-stack operator

L85@P1: Given an interesting lattice L, one of the primary problems one can consider about
L86@P1: its pop-stack operator is that of maximizing OL(x). When L is the weak order on a
L87@P1: finite irreducible Coxeter group W, Defant [7] proved that maxx∈L |OL(x)| is the Coxeter
L88@P1: number h of W; in type A, this result was originally proven much earlier by Ungar [17].
L89@P1: Defant also studied this problem for ν-Tamari lattices in [6].
L90@P1: Defant and Williams [8] found that it is fruitful to study the image of the pop-stack
L91@P1: operator when L is a semidistributive (or more generally, a semidistrim) lattice; this is
